title: rift-ds component schema
description: What one published component schema contains: the file at /schema/components/<slug>.json for every component and the chat widget. Each is generated by scripts/generate-component-schema.mjs from the props interface in the TypeScript source, through the same docgen pass that ships the .d.ts and renders Storybook's props tables, so nothing here is hand-typed. The vocabulary rules below are the data form of the contract in CLAUDE.md's Component Anatomy section; scripts/validate-prop-vocabulary.mjs owns the per-component exceptions and scripts/validate-json-schemas.mjs holds the two in step.

version.description: The rift-ds package version the schema was generated from.

kind.description: A library component, or the composed chat widget.

name.description: The exported component name, as imported.

label.description: The human name shown in navigation and page titles.

slug.description: The URL segment under /components/ and the schema file name.

category.description: A component category id from src/components/registry.json, or widget.

client.description: Whether the module declares 'use client'. A false value means the component renders from a Server Component.

importPath.description: The deep import subpath. The barrel named in barrel also re-exports it.

barrel.description: Which package barrel re-exports the module: charts modules need the optional recharts peer; chat is the widget's own subpath.

markdownUrl.description: The same contract as markdown, for pasting into an agent.

deprecated.description: Set when the component itself is deprecated: the replacement guidance.

exports.description: Every documented export of the module, the registry-named component first.

name.description: The prop name. Native attributes pass through every component and are not listed; only the component's own props are.

type.description: The resolved TypeScript type as text, literal unions expanded.

typeKind.description: The shape of the type: enum carries values; primitive is string, number or boolean; reference names a type the .d.ts defines and this schema does not expand.

values.description: The members of a literal union, sorted. Present exactly when typeKind is enum.

description.description: The prop's JSDoc description, present on every own prop by build rule.

default.description: The default as a value: a number, a boolean, null, an enum member, or a string on a prop typed as a plain string.

defaultExpression.description: Any other default as source text (a function, a computed number, a reference to another prop, or a string on a prop with a wider type).

deprecated.description: Set when the prop carries @deprecated: the replacement guidance. The prop still works; the published API only grows.

allOf.$comment: An enum lists its members, and only an enum does.
A default is a value or an expression, never both.

variant is emphasis, tone is colour. The house tones are default, neutral and destructive; the extra members are the sanctioned per-component sets in SANCTIONED_TONES in scripts/validate-prop-vocabulary.mjs, which holds the per-component rule. validate-json-schemas.mjs fails the build if this list and that script disagree.

size is not locked here: the house scale is default and compact, and the per-component scales that differ were accepted by audit and are recorded in SANCTIONED_SIZES in scripts/validate-prop-vocabulary.mjs. A size prop is a string from the component's own set.
disabled is a real boolean, never a string or a variant value.
A number, a date or a time is written in the resolved locale: the locale prop is a BCP 47 string.
A link goes through the link component, never a raw anchor: linkComponent is the LinkComponent type from the link provider.
className composes with the component's own ds- class and is always a string.

Every English string a component announces or shows is a prop with the English as its default, so it can be localised. A *Label prop is text, a function that writes text, or a union of the two, and its literal default is the English text. A boolean named for what it shows (showLabel) is a toggle, not a label, and is outside the rule.
